scope: Server ownership, release identity, assignment/media admission and at-most-once image dispatch guards. Local unit and isolated PostgreSQL-compatible database validation; no live instance or AI turn is certified by this record.

validation.command: node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=4 tests/workstation-media-upgrade-database.test.mjs tests/workstation-upgrade-database.test.mjs tests/assignment-dispatch.test.mjs tests/media-database.test.mjs tests/media-settlement.test.mjs tests/media-capacity.test.mjs tests/studio-budget-database.test.mjs

verifiedGuards: Workspace owner, employee binding, provider metadata and owned mirror must agree before lifecycle operations.
A Craft target requires exact template revision and immutable image digest. Fresh instances also require the selected release identity.
Only server-owned previous releases can migrate. A legacy null digest is accepted only with an exact known old template revision; completion still requires the target digest through GET.
Only a current running assignment with idle dispatch, current generation and active project can claim and dispatch an image update.
A persistent dispatch receipt precedes the provider POST. Lost replies, transport errors, time and provider drift never authorize another POST.
Another unresolved image target blocks reconciliation even when the current GET already matches the desired target.
Pending and dispatched image receipts block new AI turns. Pending plans retain employee readiness for existing paid media recovery; provisioning starts at actual image dispatch.
Active or financially unsettled media protects its owned instance, including unbound jobs attributed to the employee or its legacy payer identity.

Late legacy binding, revival and reservation serialize against image dispatch. Token-bound creation retains its existing assignment lock order; current Director reservations and financial settlement remain available.
Only never-dispatched plans can be superseded. Unresolved provider receipts survive assignment deletion.
Reconciliation changes only the owned mirror template. Instance identity, resources and caps are preserved; the provider update body contains only the selected template.
Research retains its existing versioned workstation contract. Explicit legacy media recovery may retain a known previous image without authorizing an image update.
limits: No live same-ID image migration, home-file preservation or managed-client activation was executed by this validation. Those require a separate operator canary record.
Unknown outcomes intentionally remain fenced for operator reconciliation. No timeout-based reset or blind retry is provided.
This record does not certify publication or deployment of a matching web/runtime release. The release record must supply final commits, editor pins and managed-client identity.
